output.brief: The evidence does not support the claim as drafted. The platform's audit trail, which users can't edit, shows the architect answered 62 of 64 queries within the contract period. The "late" queries in the claim were measured from when Callerby opened its own drafts, and 39 of the 41 sat in Callerby's drafts for 9–47 days. The structural query on CO-09 was answered in four days. Meanwhile the tower crane left in October 2025 and came back in April 2026. It went to the Kestrel job, and the site diaries record the frame as "on hold – design" throughout. Gareth's own report described the crane's removal as cost-saving. So Callerby's redeployment of the crane is the best-supported cause. Whether the change orders, especially CO-09, cost any time is still unknown. Do not submit the claim as drafted on 1 December, since it would rest on a misleading measure. Do not discipline the superintendent, who answered honestly. Do not suspend the incentive scheme yet, because the link to the crane move is unproven. Next, commission an independent delay analysis, with a fee not tied to the amount recovered. It should test CO-09's real effect and Callerby's own share of the delay. Then decide whether to submit a narrower claim or settle. I'm moderately confident in this, not fully.
